newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital market closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital market closing report.

text.p: The 10-year French bond future contract settled lower but fared better than U.S. Treasuries on the back of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's warning of a a pre-emptive U.S. monetary policy tightening.
"The notionnel and the Bund held up well despite the deterioration of the U.S. market," said one analyst.
Greenspan delivered an upbeat assessment of the U.S. economy but voiced concern about skyrocketing stock prices and the risk of higher inflation.
The bond future touched a low of 131.86 just after Greenspan's comments but then retraced some of its losses to settle at 132.00, down 22 basis points, close to the top of the day's trading range.
Analysts said the notionnel was expected to continue its consolidation on Thursday. One cited intermediate support at 131.80 and with the next downside stop 131.54/50.
March PIBOR finished lower, losing two basis points to settle at 96.63. One analyst said the market was rattled by comments by Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke.
Welteke said that the mark could not continue to depreciate against the dollar at the pace seen over the past few days.
Analysts said that they did not expect the Bank of France to ease rates after Thursday's regular monetary policy council meeting.
Three-month money market rates tightened to 3.23/3.32 percent against 3.22/3.29 percent on Tuesday.
